findings.reason: without a node field in the key the sweep either prunes a live remote host's directory (re-introducing the duplicate lift §51 fixed) or prunes nothing, so §52 must name the node signal (the `socket.gethostname()` convention `follower_registration` and `checkout_trust` already use) or change the rule.
findings.text: §52 says "A host on another node is never judged dead from this node" while also deciding liveness by pid together with start tick, but §51's key is `host-<pid>-<start>` with no node field, so a pid absent locally reads the same whether the host died on this node or runs elsewhere; the builder cannot satisfy both "the dead host's directory removed" and "a foreign host is kept" from the signal the plan names

findings.reason: the only case guarding the cross-node rule cannot fail, so §52's gate would close on a sweep that prunes foreign hosts' directories.
findings.text: §52's done-when asserts the case "a directory whose recorded host cannot be checked on this node is also kept" as the guard for the cross-node invariant, but every parseable `host-<pid>-<start>` is checkable the same way, so no seeded tree can put a directory into the "cannot be checked" state and the case passes however the sweep behaves

findings.reason: the selector the section is built on does not hold across the reload path §21 exists to cover, so §51 needs either a host-only stamp the follower never writes itself or a reload case in its done-when.
findings.text: §51's Deliverable states "A follower is hosted exactly when `RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER` is present in its environment", but the follower's own reloader stamps that exact variable into its replacement image unconditionally: `owner = runs_module.follower_owner()` is always a tuple (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:3113`), and the re-exec writes it whenever `self.owner is not None` (`:572-575`), and `lift_claim_key` reads the raw `os.environ` value (`git show a17720af7:reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1184`), so an unhosted follower that has reloaded once presents the variable and takes the host key rather than the per-session key the Deliverable promises
